tweets.title: The Ministry of Defence (MoD) has notified the 6th Positive Indigenisation List, banning the import of 405 strategically vital defence components. Sourced exclusively from domestic manufacturers, the initiative carries an estimated business value of ₹3,070 crore to bolster national self-reliance. The list targets sub-systems and line-replaceable units (LRUs) for frontline military assets, including gears for light combat helicopters, T-72/T-90 tanks, LCA Tejas, and Su-30MKI fighter jets. US AIR FORCE BUYS CHINESE DJI DRONES; FOR NUCLEAR BASE DEFENCE TRAINING

The U.S. Air Force is procuring DJI drones to train counter-UAS personnel at F.E. Warren Air Force Base, one of the three bases hosting Minuteman III ICBMs.

The procurement reportedly includes refurbished DJI Mavic 2 Pro, Mini 3 Pro and Avata 2 systems.

Why Chinese drones? The Air Force says DJI dominates the commercial drone market and its drones have proprietary RF signatures, protocols and flight characteristics that U.S.-made systems cannot fully replicate.

The drones will be used in exercises involving radar, electronic warfare and other counter-drone systems.

To mitigate security risks, the aircraft will reportedly be modified with RIZER software and operated in an air-gapped configuration to prevent sensitive telemetry or imagery from being transmitted externally.
